_note: Hand-edited source of truth for tarot/sources/grammar.json (built by scripts/build_sources_grammar.py). One entry per place where pictures of a deck can be found. Checked Oct 19-20 2026 by Claude for PlayfulProcess. 'rights_published' is the holder's own words where they could be read; where a site blocked automated reading, the entry says so and gives what a search summary showed. 'image' is set only where the source's own statement says public domain, CC0 or CC BY. Not legal advice.

rights_classes.free: Free for any use, as the holder states (public domain, CC0, or an open-access policy)
rights_classes.open-licence: Open licence with conditions (credit, keep the licence)
rights_classes.unclear: No rights statement found, or the scan's origin is unclear
rights_classes.in-copyright: In copyright: link and cite only

holders.morgan: The Morgan Library & Museum, New York
holders.carrara: Accademia Carrara and the Colleoni collection, Bergamo
holders.publishers: Publishers of modern decks and books
holders.lacma: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

sources.title: The Equinox I(8), 1912: Book T, the printed text (scan)
sources.holder_name: Internet Archive, IAPSOP collection (item IAPSOP-equinox_v1_n8_1912_Sep)
sources.holds: The whole September 1912 issue, with Book T on pp. 143-210. Text only: Book T as printed has no card pictures.
sources.quality: Page scans with OCR; good enough to check every word of the transcription (this site's Book T text was checked against it).
sources.rights_published: The item's metadata carries no rights statement (checked Oct 20 2026 through archive.org/metadata). The work is public domain: printed 1912, Crowley died 1947, Mathers 1918.
sources.property_rights: Nobody holds rights in the 1912 text; the scan carries no terms. We may quote, reprint and adapt Book T's words; this site does.

sources.title: Book T transcriptions: the-equinox.org and sacred-texts
sources.holder_name: the-equinox.org (Equinox I(8) transcription); sacred-texts.com (Mathers, The Tarot, 1888)
sources.holds: Book T 1912 retyped (the base of this site's text), and Mathers' separate 1888 booklet The Tarot at https://sacred-texts.com/tarot/mathers/index.htm.
sources.quality: Text only, no pictures. Retyped, so check doubtful words against the scan.
sources.rights_published: The underlying texts are public domain (1888, 1912). The transcription sites' own terms were not checked for this entry.
sources.property_rights: The words are free to use; the sites' retyping and markup are theirs, so we copy from the 1912 scan, not their pages.

sources.title: Whare Ra trump line drawings (Hermetic Library)
sources.holder_name: Hermetic Library, Golden Dawn Library Project; drawings courtesy of Pat Zalewski
sources.holds: Black-and-white line drawings of the 22 trumps as kept at Whare Ra (New Zealand, 1912-1978), the longest-lived Golden Dawn temple. Minors listed as forthcoming.
sources.quality: Web images of line drawings; seen in search summaries only (the site blocks automated reading).
sources.rights_published: No statement could be read (site blocks automated reading). The drawings are presented as courtesy of Pat Zalewski.
sources.property_rights: Treat as held by Pat Zalewski and the Hermetic Library: link to them; reproducing the drawings needs their permission.

sources.title: Yorke Collection and the Thoth paintings (Warburg Institute)
sources.holder_name: Warburg Institute Archive, University of London
sources.holds: Gerald Yorke's collection of Crowley and Golden Dawn papers (Cypher manuscripts, Order documents; catalogues in two series, OS and NS), and Lady Frieda Harris's original Thoth paintings (1938-1943). Whether a manuscript Book T or a painted Order deck is among the papers was not confirmed.
sources.quality: Originals, seen by appointment in the reading room; the catalogue lists are PDFs (e.g. https://warburg.sas.ac.uk/sites/default/files/Yorke%20Collection%20NS%201%20-%2049.pdf).
sources.rights_published: The archive page says permission to view the manuscripts must be requested in advance. No image licence was found online.
sources.property_rights: The papers belong to the Warburg; Crowley's and Harris's work is still in copyright in the UK (Harris d. 1962). Ask the Warburg, and the rights holders, before any reproduction.

sources.title: W. B. Yeats occult papers (National Library of Ireland)
sources.holder_name: National Library of Ireland
sources.holds: Yeats's Golden Dawn papers, ca. 1890-1937, including astrological and tarot material. Whether a hand-painted deck is among them is unconfirmed; Kathleen Raine's Yeats, the Tarot and the Golden Dawn (1972) is the published study.
sources.quality: Originals; catalogue only online (it blocks automated reading).
sources.rights_published: No statement could be read (catalogue blocks automated reading).
sources.property_rights: Held by the NLI; Yeats's own papers are out of copyright (d. 1939), the library's images are under its terms. Ask the NLI.

sources.title: Published Golden Dawn decks (Wang, Dowson, the Ciceros, the Zalewskis) and the Thoth
sources.holder_name: U.S. Games Systems (Wang/Regardie 1977-78; Dowson's Hermetic Tarot 1980); Llewellyn (the Ciceros, 1991 and later); the Zalewskis' Magical Tarot of the Golden Dawn (2022); the Thoth (Crowley/Harris, O.T.O.)
sources.holds: The modern decks painted from the Order's descriptions, several under Regardie's oversight. Steve P.'s pages compare them card by card; Nick Farrell's essay (https://www.jwmt.org/v2n17/farrell.html) argues the Order never had a deck of its own.
sources.quality: Printed decks; reviews and comparison scans on reference sites.
sources.rights_published: All are in copyright. No open licence found for any of them.
sources.property_rights: Each publisher holds its deck. We may name, describe and link them; we may not copy their pictures.

sources.title: The Golden Dawn Court Cards (Küntz, ed., 1996)
sources.holder_name: Holmes Publishing Group (Golden Dawn Studies 5)
sources.holds: Line drawings of the court cards from W. Wynn Westcott's papers, credited to Westcott and/or Moina Mathers. The nearest thing to Order-made court pictures in print. Not seen here (listings only).
sources.quality: Printed book.
sources.rights_published: No statement read; the edition is in copyright. Whether the underlying drawings (before 1900, makers d. 1925 and 1928) are themselves free is a question of who owns the originals.
sources.property_rights: The book is Holmes's; the original drawings' owner is not named online. Cite and link only.

sources.title: Rider-Waite-Smith on Wikimedia Commons (the scans this site shows)
sources.holder_name: Wikimedia Commons, Category:Rider-Waite tarot deck (files credited to muzendo.jp)
sources.holds: All 78 cards, scanned from an early printing whose edition is not recorded.
sources.quality: About 1,100 x 1,900 px per card.
sources.rights_published: Each file page: "Public domain". The tag is the uploader's statement about the work (Smith's 1909 designs, public domain in the US, and in the UK/EU since 2022).
sources.property_rights: Smith's 1909 pictures are free; RIDER-WAITE is a U.S. Games trademark for printed tarot cards, so keep that word off anything for sale.
sources.image_credit: Pamela Colman Smith, 1909; Wikimedia Commons, public domain

sources.holds: 80 files: the 78 cards of the December 1909 first run, which had a roses-and-lilies back pattern, plus back and pack.
sources.quality: 812-860 px wide: smaller than the scans this site shows, but the right printing.
sources.rights_published: Each of the 80 file pages: "Public domain" (checked through the Commons API, Oct 19 2026).
sources.property_rights: Free to use. The scans' owner is a private collector; credit the blog as Commons does.
sources.image_credit: Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 first printing; Wikimedia Commons, public domain

sources.title: A Waite-Smith deck at Yale (10 cards on Commons)
sources.holder_name: Wikimedia Commons, Category:Rider-Waite tarot deck (Yale University)
sources.holds: 10 cards photographed from a Yale copy; which printing is not stated in the category.
sources.quality: About 1,810-1,870 px wide: the sharpest Waite-Smith scans found, for ten cards.
sources.rights_published: Commons file pages carry public-domain tags (licence not re-checked file by file for this entry).

sources.title: The early editions compared (World of Playing Cards)
sources.holder_name: The World of Playing Cards (wopc.co.uk); Pam-A and Pam-D images courtesy Kenji Ishimatsu
sources.holds: How to tell the 1909 first edition and the Pam-A (1910-c.1920), Pam-C, Pam-D and Pam-B printings apart: line, colour, lettering, thickness, box, book.
sources.quality: Comparison images, web size.
sources.rights_published: No image-use statement on the page; its only related line credits the images to Kenji Ishimatsu.
sources.property_rights: The photographs are the collector's: link to the page, don't copy them. Use it to identify which printing a free scan shows.

sources.title: d'Este cards at Yale: full-resolution IIIF
sources.holder_name: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library, Yale: Cary Collection, PLAYING CARDS GEN 966 (record 33215685)
sources.holds: All 16 surviving cards, fronts and backs (32 images). Yale's record: "Imperfect: 16 cards only", "[1450?]", 140 x 78 mm, hand coloured, embossing, "Composition of deck unknown". IIIF manifest: https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/33215685
sources.quality: Full size 3,256 x 5,640 px per card (IIIF level 2; TIFF, JPG, PNG). This site shows 1,100 x 1,905 px: Yale's own files are about three times sharper in each direction.
sources.rights_published: The record: "The use of this image may be subject to the copyright law of the United States (Title 17, United States Code) or to site license or other rights management terms and conditions. The person using the image is liable for any infringement." Provider: "Yale University Library". Yale's open-access policy (guides.library.yale.edu/openaccess): "Open access digital images may be used by anyone for any purpose." It covers works believed public domain; "The policy does not apply to works protected by copyright, by privacy rights, or that are otherwise restricted."
sources.property_rights: Yale owns the cards; the 15th-century paintings are public domain and Yale's policy lets anyone use its open-access images for any purpose, with "Yale University Library" as provider. We may show, print and sell them; credit Yale.

sources.title: d'Este cards discussed: trionfi.com, Pollett, Into Mystery
sources.holder_name: trionfi.com (16 d'Este cards); Andy Pollett, The Tarots of Ferrara; Into Mystery (Substack)
sources.holds: Identifications and dating arguments: the Este arms on the court cards (Ercole I d'Este and Eleonora of Aragon, hence c. 1473 rather than c. 1450), the Star's figures. Also http://trionfi.com/0/j/d/16Este/ and https://l-pollett.tripod.com/cards84.htm.
sources.quality: Web-size images taken from Yale or older photographs.
sources.rights_published: No image licence on these pages (trionfi.com could not be opened, Oct 20 2026).
sources.property_rights: Their texts and layouts are theirs; the card pictures should come from Yale, not from them.

sources.title: Related: the Rothschild cards at the Louvre
sources.holder_name: Musée du Louvre, Département des Arts graphiques, Collection Edmond de Rothschild
sources.holds: A hand-painted 15th-century pack of about 31 cards (one more at Bassano del Grappa), sometimes discussed beside the Ferrarese cards; the Louvre's 2026 notice dates it Florence c. 1435-1440. Not the d'Este pack: listed here for comparison only.
sources.quality: Louvre collections site images with a download button (collections.louvre.fr).
sources.rights_published: Image caption: "© GrandPalaisRmn (Musée du Louvre) / Tony Querrec"; download requires "I accept the Terms and conditions".
sources.property_rights: The photographs are GrandPalaisRmn's. Link only, unless the Louvre's terms say otherwise.

sources.title: Cary-Yale (Visconti di Modrone) cards at Yale: IIIF
sources.holder_name: Beinecke, Cary Collection, PLAYING CARDS GEN 965 (record 33220491)
sources.holds: The 67 surviving cards, fronts and backs (134 images); Yale dates them "[between 1442 and 1447]".
sources.quality: Full-resolution IIIF; Commons copies of the same cards range from 457 to 9,328 px wide, so check each card for the largest.
sources.rights_published: Same record statement as the d'Este cards: "The use of this image may be subject to the copyright law of the United States (Title 17, United States Code) or to site license or other rights management terms and conditions. The person using the image is liable for any infringement." Yale's open-access policy: "Open access digital images may be used by anyone for any purpose."
sources.property_rights: As for the d'Este cards: public-domain work, Yale's open-access images free for any use; credit Yale University Library.

sources.holder_name: Wikimedia Commons, Category:Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot (credit: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library)

sources.quality: Web size; Yale's IIIF is the better copy.
sources.rights_published: File pages: "Public domain" (from the Oct 4 2026 ledger, docs/rights/IMAGE-LEDGER.md).
sources.property_rights: Free to use; credit the Beinecke.
sources.image_credit: Bonifacio Bembo workshop, c. 1442-47; Beinecke Library, Yale; Wikimedia Commons, public domain

sources.title: Visconti-Sforza cards at the Morgan (MS M.630)
sources.holder_name: The Morgan Library & Museum, New York, MS M.630.1-35 (purchased by J. Pierpont Morgan, 1911)
sources.holds: 35 of the deck's 74 surviving cards, each with its own page and a download button.
sources.quality: Low-resolution downloads on the site; high resolution only through Imaging & Rights (photoservices@themorgan.org).
sources.rights_published: From the Morgan's copyright notice (themorgan.org/node/7; the site blocks automated reading, so this is the wording a search engine shows): images may be downloaded for personal, educational or noncommercial use, and "Images must remain unaltered; the accompanying description must include artist, author or composer, title, date, accession number and collection credit." Publication or commercial use needs the Morgan's written permission and fees.
sources.property_rights: The Morgan holds its photographs. On this free site, unaltered and fully captioned, the downloads may be shown; anything for sale or cropped needs the Morgan.

sources.title: Visconti-Sforza cards in Bergamo (Accademia Carrara; Colleoni collection)
sources.holder_name: Accademia Carrara (26 cards, Baglioni bequest 1900) and the private Colleoni collection (13 cards), Bergamo
sources.holds: The other 39 cards of the Morgan-Bergamo deck. The Carrara and the Morgan showed them together in 2026 (Tarocchi: le origini, le carte, la fortuna).
sources.quality: No online collection images found. The National Gallery of Australia's exhibition pages show some Carrara cards (digital.nga.gov.au).
sources.rights_published: No image statement found online (Oct 20 2026).
sources.property_rights: The Carrara and the Colleoni family own their cards. Italian heritage law can charge fees for commercial reproduction of works in public collections; ask the museum.

sources.title: Visconti-Sforza on Wikimedia Commons (the images this site shows)
sources.holder_name: Wikimedia Commons, Category:Pierpont Morgan-Bergamo Visconti-Sforza Tarot
sources.holds: 87 card scans credited "scanned by David Madore" (the credit adds that they are scans of a facsimile printed by AGMüller in Switzerland) and 23 trumps credited "Scanned from the Dal Negro reproduction: I Tarocchi dei Visconti". So every Visconti-Sforza picture this site shows is a copy of a modern facsimile.
sources.quality: About 360 x 720 px (Dal Negro) and 512 x 1,024 px (Madore): copies of printed facsimiles, not the cards.
sources.rights_published: File pages: "Public domain" (the uploader's statement about the 15th-century work).
sources.property_rights: The work is free. A flat copy of a facsimile adds no new copyright in the US or (since 2019) the EU, but these are a printer's colours, not Bembo's. Prefer the Morgan's own images for its 35 cards.

sources.title: Visconti-Sforza cards photographed at the Morgan (Commons)
sources.holder_name: Wikimedia Commons: visitor photographs 'shot at the library' (Fool, Queen and King of Swords, Three of Swords, Seven of Coins, a mounted Queen); and the Popess (File:Bonifacio Bembo.jpg, credited to trionfi.com)
sources.holds: Photographs of the real cards, not a facsimile, for six cards; one more (the Popess) copied from trionfi.com.
sources.quality: Tiny: about 170-180 px wide (Popess 300 px).
sources.rights_published: File pages: "Own work", "Public domain" (the Popess: "Public domain", credit trionfi.com).
sources.property_rights: The photographers released them; free for any use. Too small for anything but a thumbnail or a colour check.

sources.title: Related: the Brambilla Visconti cards at Brera
sources.holder_name: Wikimedia Commons, Category:Visconti-Sforza tarot deck cards in the Pinacoteca di Brera
sources.holds: The Brambilla deck, 48 cards bought by the Italian state in 1971 for Brera: a third Visconti pack, not shown on this site.
sources.quality: As uploaded; not measured.
sources.rights_published: Commons file pages' tags (not re-checked file by file for this entry).
sources.property_rights: The cards are state property at Brera; the Commons photographs carry their uploaders' statements.

sources.title: The 'Charles VI' cards at the BnF (Gallica)
sources.holder_name: Bibliothèque nationale de France, Estampes et photographie, RESERVE BOITE ECU-KH-24 (from Roger de Gaignières's collection)
sources.holds: The 17 surviving hand-painted cards; this site shows them via the BnF's online exhibition and Commons. The BnF catalogue record: https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb409180334 (Gallica ark not confirmed here).
sources.quality: About 300 x 600 px on this site; Gallica's own viewer is sharper.
sources.rights_published: Gallica's conditions of use, as printed on its documents: the credit "Source gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France" (or "Source gallica.bnf.fr / BnF") for free non-commercial reuse, and "La réutilisation commerciale de ces contenus est payante et fait l'objet d'une licence." (Commercial reuse of these contents is paid and needs a licence.)
sources.property_rights: The BnF owns the cards and charges for commercial use of its scans. Fine on this free site with the credit; a printed deck needs a BnF licence.

sources.title: The 'Charles VI' cards in colour lithograph, 1844 (Société des bibliophiles français)
sources.holder_name: Université de Liège, DONum digital library (copy of Jeux de cartes tarots et de cartes numérales du quatorzième au dix-huitième siècle, Paris, Crapelet, 1844)
sources.holds: 100 plates, opening with all seventeen 'Gringonneur' cards "engraved in lithography, and carefully coloured by hand after the original drawings" (Chatto, 1848, describing this book). A 19th-century copy of the cards, not a photograph of them.
sources.quality: One open-access PDF of the whole book (50.5 MB); plate resolution not measured.
sources.rights_published: The record sits in DONum's "Public domain" collection; the site's general line: "Items in DONum are protected by copyright, with all rights reserved, unless otherwise indicated."
sources.property_rights: The 1844 plates are public domain and Liège files the scan as public domain: the one free-for-any-use source found for all 17 cards. A copy of a copy: say so on the card.

sources.title: Chatto, Facts and Speculations on the Origin and History of Playing Cards (1848)
sources.holder_name: Internet Archive and Project Gutenberg (ebook 45584); Commons holds its plates as 'History of Playing Cards (1848) NN.png'
sources.holds: Black-and-white engravings of two 'Gringonneur' cards, La Justice and La Lune (p. 198), and a list of all seventeen.
sources.quality: Book engravings; Commons plate files about 1,500 x 2,950 px.
sources.rights_published: Internet Archive item factsandspeculat45584gut: possible-copyright-status "NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT"; Commons plate pages: "Public domain".
sources.property_rights: Free for any use. Two cards only, in line, not colour.

sources.title: Sola Busca at the Pinacoteca di Brera (the only complete set)
sources.holder_name: Pinacoteca di Brera, Milan (bought by the Italian Ministry of Culture in 2009)
sources.holds: All 78 hand-coloured engraved cards, c. 1491, described by Brera as the oldest complete tarot deck.
sources.quality: No high-resolution online set found; licensed facsimiles (e.g. Lo Scarabeo, under licence from Brera) exist.
sources.rights_published: No image licence found on Brera's pages (Oct 20 2026).
sources.property_rights: State property. Italy's heritage code (art. 108) lets the state charge for commercial reproductions of works it holds; an Italian court applied it to a foreign puzzle maker in 2022. Ask Brera before any sale.

sources.quality: Large downloads from the collection site.
sources.rights_published: BM image pages: "Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)", credit "© The Trustees of the British Museum"; commercial use through BM Images (sales@bmimages.com).
sources.property_rights: The BM licenses its photographs non-commercially. Usable here with the credit and share-alike; not in anything sold.
